vulnerabilities.description: Unbounded RUNS list memory accumulation in long-lived systemd process. The RUNS list (lines 68-69) appends job execution records indefinitely without trimming. While the HTTP response filters to last 30 runs (line 879), the in-memory list grows unbounded over weeks of uptime (3 syncs/day × weeks = hundreds of run objects). Each Run object holds step logs and metadata.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: RUNS list accumulates unbounded records, never trimmed in systemd process
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Run paceforge-runner for 60 days with 3 syncs/day = 180+ run records in memory. Process memory grows linearly; after 1 year could consume hundreds of MB
vulnerabilities.impact: Memory exhaustion on long-lived runner; restart required to reclaim memory
vulnerabilities.reproduction: Monitor RUNS list size: len(RUNS) after 1+ months of continuous operation
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add max-size cap to RUNS list (e.g., keep last 200 runs in memory only, older ones disk-only via runs.jsonl)

vulnerabilities.description: Loose dependency version constraints allow automatic updates that could introduce vulnerabilities. Most dependencies use >= without upper bound (pydantic>=2.0, httpx>=0.27, beautifulsoup4>=4.11.0, etc.). While ruff is pinned (line 25: >=0.15,<0.16), core dependencies lack version stability.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Dependencies unpinned to specific versions; auto-updates risk security regression
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: New pydantic or beautifulsoup4 version ships with breaking changes or vulnerabilities. Next pip install pulls it silently, breaking features or opening attack surface
vulnerabilities.impact: Unexpected breaking changes, security regression in transitive dependencies
vulnerabilities.remediation: Pin major.minor versions: pydantic>=2.0,<3 or use lock file (requirements.txt, Poetry.lock)

vulnerabilities.description: XML entity expansion uncapped in parseXml() and decodeEntities(). The hand-rolled XML parser handles named/numeric entities but lacks depth limits or entity count bounds. A malicious ZWO (Zwift workout) file with deeply nested entity definitions could trigger DoS during parsing.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Unbounded XML entity expansion in ZWO file parser
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Upload ZWO file with nested entity expansion (billion laughs attack). Parser allocates unbounded memory or runs longest without timeout
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of service; browser tab becomes unresponsive during ride load
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add entity expansion depth limit (max 10 levels); count unique entity definitions

vulnerabilities.description: No CSRF token validation on state-changing POST endpoints. Endpoints at /run/*, /gh/repos/*/actions/workflows/*/dispatches, and /gh/repos/*/issues accept authenticated POST requests without CSRF tokens. A logged-in user visiting an attacker-controlled site could trigger unwanted plan changes, Garmin syncs, or coach tasks.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: State-changing POST operations lack CSRF token validation
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: User logged into /paceforge/ visits attacker.com which embeds: . Attacker triggers job dispatch without user intent
vulnerabilities.impact: Unauthorized state changes (plan mutations, Garmin calendar reconciliation, coach tasks)
vulnerabilities.remediation: Generate CSRF tokens on login, require validation in POST body (or use SameSite=Strict on session cookie as defense)

vulnerabilities.description: No rate limiting on bike ride uploads to external services (intervals.icu, Strava). uploadIntervalsIcu() and uploadStrava() have no throttling or retry backoff. A malicious script could spam uploads without limit.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Unthrottled FIT uploads to intervals.icu and Strava
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: Browser console loop: for(let i=0;i<100;i++) uploadIntervalsIcu(fitBytes, {apiKey, name}). Floods external service; IP may be rate-limited or blocked by target
vulnerabilities.impact: DoS against external services, potential IP blocking
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add client-side upload queue with throttle (1 upload per 5 minutes); show upload status

vulnerabilities.description: SVG color values injected directly into style attributes without validation. In profileShapes() function, color from step.zone is interpolated into SVG polygon fill and CSS color-mix() without sanitization. Currently safe because colors are from hardcoded COGGAN_ZONES, but future user-controllable colors could allow CSS injection.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: SVG color values injected unsanitized into style attributes
vulnerabilities.failure_scenario: If step.zone becomes user-input, attacker sets zone to CSS payload: url('https://attacker/') or other injection. Injects attacker content into rendered page
vulnerabilities.impact: CSS injection potential; low risk if only internal zones, high if ever user-controlled
vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate color values against /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/ regex; use CSS custom properties instead of interpolation

good_practices.finding: Password hashing uses scrypt with constant-time comparison
good_practices.detail: check_login() uses scrypt(n=2^14, r=8, p=1) with hmac.compare_digest() for timing-safe comparison. Prevents timing attacks and brute-force.

good_practices.finding: Session cookies configured with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax
good_practices.detail: Set-Cookie includes all three flags. HttpOnly prevents XSS token theft; Secure enforces HTTPS; SameSite=Lax mitigates most CSRF.

good_practices.finding: No database = no SQL injection surface
good_practices.detail: File-based JSON storage (data/*.json) eliminates SQL injection attack surface entirely.

good_practices.finding: HTTP body size limit prevents DoS on unauthenticated endpoint
good_practices.detail: MAX_BODY = 1 MiB; _body() caps read at min(Content-Length, MAX_BODY) to prevent unbounded allocation on /auth/login.

good_practices.finding: Path traversal protections using is_relative_to() checks
good_practices.detail: File-serving endpoints verify resolved path is within REPO_DIR/web or REPO_DIR/data. Prevents ../../../etc/passwd attacks.

good_practices.finding: Garmin credentials never persisted or logged
good_practices.detail: Credentials held only during handshake (in-memory); tokens stored only in token dir; passwords never logged.

good_practices.finding: HTML entity escaping in Telegram notifications
good_practices.detail: telegram() function escapes <, >, & before sending to prevent HTML injection.

good_practices.finding: Global rate limiting on failed login attempts
good_practices.detail: _LOGIN_BRAKE serializes failed-login sleeps. 1s sleep per attempt prevents rapid brute-force.

not_applicable: Hardcoded secrets in code (secrets in env file only, not committed)
Remote code execution (no eval/exec of user input)
XXE attacks (XML parser handles only basic entities; no DOCTYPE/SYSTEM support)
risk_score_summary: Low-to-Medium. No high-severity vulnerabilities; 2 medium (RUNS memory leak, loose dependencies); 4 low. Mitigated by: file-based storage, scrypt auth, secure cookies, path traversal checks.
summary: PaceForge backend (runner.py) is security-conscious: scrypt auth, secure cookies, path traversal guards, input validation, and no database eliminate SQL injection. Frontend bike modules properly escape HTML. Main issues are architectural (unbounded RUNS list in long-running systemd) and operational (loose dependency pins). Low-severity findings are present but context-mitigated (XML parsing on user uploads, CSRF requires active session).
recommendations: 1. Add max-size cap to RUNS list (keep last 200, archive older to disk). Trim after append.
2. Pin dependency versions: pydantic>=2.0,<3; httpx>=0.27,<0.28; etc. Use Poetry.lock.
3. Add CSRF tokens to state-changing POST endpoints. Generate on login, validate before dispatch.
4. Cap XML entity expansion: track depth (max 10) and unique entities (max 100).
5. Add client-side upload queue on intervals.icu/Strava with 5min throttle.
6. Whitelist SVG colors; validate against /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/ regex.
